Amanda Peet is 5 feet 6 inches tall with a slim frame and long limbs, and for most of the 2000s that combination placed her repeatedly in romantic-lead and best-friend roles. Over time, though, she moved well beyond that typecast image. In 2021, she took a major step behind the camera when she co-created The Chair for Netflix and cast Sandra Oh in the lead role.

StreamIndie Films

Amanda Peet was born on 11 January 1972 in New York City. Her mother, Penny Levy, was a social worker, while her father, Charles Peet Jr., was a corporate lawyer. They divorced when she was young, and she grew up with an older sister who became a doctor.

Rather than entering acting through a conventional child-star route, Peet came into the profession through education. She attended Friends Seminary in Manhattan before studying American history at Columbia University. While at Columbia, she trained with renowned acting teacher Uta Hagen. She graduated in 1994, began appearing in commercials, and made her film debut the following year.

Who Is Amanda Peet’s Husband?

Amanda Peet is married to David Benioff, the novelist and screenwriter who co-created Game of Thrones and 3 Body Problem.

A mutual friend, the screenwriter Peter Blake, set them up on a blind date. They married on 30 September 2006 in a private Jewish ceremony and have three children.

Before Benioff, Peet was briefly linked to John F. Kennedy Jr. in 1994, dated Ben Stiller in the late 1990s, and was with the actor Brian Van Holt from 2001 to 2003.

Has Amanda Peet Had Plastic Surgery?

StreamShows

Peet has never had cosmetic surgery, and she has been unusually direct about the fact that she keeps considering it.

She told NPR in 2026 that a facelift crosses her mind constantly, and that plenty of her friends have had one while plenty have not. She has explained that her cancer diagnosis influenced her decision not to undergo any surgery that was not medically needed.

How Her Look Shaped Her Casting

Through the 2000s, Peet was frequently cast as the romantic lead or the likeable best friend. Films such as The Whole Nine Yards, Saving Silverman, A Lot Like Love, and Something’s Gotta Give placed her within that familiar screen type.

Her later work increasingly moved away from those expectations. Roles such as Betty Broderick in Dirty John, Beth Gallagher in Fatal Attraction, and Mel Cooper in Your Friends & Neighbors gave her characters with considerably more complexity and sharper edges.

Amanda Peet’s Breast Cancer Diagnosis

Peet revealed in an essay for The New Yorker on 21 March 2026, titled “My Season of Ativan”, that she had been diagnosed with Stage I breast cancer in the autumn of 2025.

StreamShows

She had previously been told that she had dense breast tissue and had been seeing a breast surgeon regularly. During what she expected to be a routine examination, an ultrasound revealed an area that required further investigation. A biopsy subsequently confirmed the diagnosis.

She was treated with a lumpectomy and radiation and did not need chemotherapy. Her first clear scan came in mid-January 2026.

Amanda Peet Career Highlights:

Breaking Through

Peet began her professional career with television commercials before moving into small television and film roles during the 1990s. Early credits included appearances on Seinfeld, Spin City, and Law & Order, along with films such as She’s the One, One Fine Day, and Playing by Heart.

Her first substantial role was Jacqueline Barrett on the WB series Jack & Jill from 1999, which is where she met Sarah Paulson.

The Whole Nine Yards and the 2000s

The 2000 comedy made her a recognizable Hollywood actress and opened a decade of steady studio work: Saving Silverman, Changing Lanes, High Crimes, Igby Goes Down, Identity, Melinda and Melinda, A Lot Like Love, Syriana, The X-Files: I Want to Believe, and the disaster film 2012.

StreamIndie Films

Television remained important as well. She played Jordan McDeere in Aaron Sorkin’s Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip in 2006 and earned an Independent Spirit Award nomination for Please Give in 2010.

Television and More Complex Roles

The 2010s moved her toward television and toward characters with sharper edges. She starred in the Duplass brothers’ Togetherness for two seasons, played Jules on Brockmire, appeared in The Romanoffs, and took the title role in Dirty John: The Betty Broderick Story in 2020. She followed it as Beth Gallagher in Paramount+’s Fatal Attraction in 2023.

Writing and Producing

She expanded her creative work beyond acting with the 2013 play The Commons of Pensacola. She later wrote Our Very Own Carlin McCullough, commissioned and premiered by the Geffen Playhouse in 2018.

StreamIndie Films

Her most visible behind-the-scenes achievement came with The Chair. Released on Netflix in August 2021, the series was created by Peet and Annie Julia Wyman. Peet co-wrote the pilot and served as an executive producer alongside David Benioff, D.B. Weiss, and Sandra Oh, who also starred in the series.
